alex_m: Heads up — saw a p99 spike during yesterday's lunch burst (~12:15 UTC). Scale-up lag ~50s, p99 jumped ~2.3x. Quick profiling shows kernel_selector falling back and kv cache miss rate spiking. Paste of the relevant log snippet below:

```
kernel_selector: layer=22 picked=generic_kernel reason=no_optimized_variant
kernel_selector: layer=23 picked=generic_kernel reason=no_optimized_variant
kv_cache: miss_count=320 window=120s (baseline 18)
runtime: microbatch_size=8 observed during 12:14:30-12:16:10
agent: scaleup_start=12:14:20 scaleup_ready=12:15:12
```

Anyone else see the same pattern or have immediate mitigation ideas?

deploy-bot: Deployed release v2.14.3 at 2026-03-16T11:58:47Z

jia_w: I saw this too in the rollout dashboard. Looks like a CI change disabled cpu-tile-opt flags for the tiled kernels — that would explain optimized kernels not matching.

sam_runtime: Confirming from perf samples — we get more time in the generic codepath when microbatch increases. The autoscaler queueing means requests are batched up to 8, which hurts long-seq models. Quick metric query: `histogram_max(batch_size)` shows a spike in batch size during the event.

maya_r: KV cache cold misses are a huge factor. New replicas start with empty prefix cache so first few requests pay the full KV build cost per token. During a burst with many new replicas we see miss amplification. Suggestion: prewarm KV or seed with popular prefixes on scale-up. :thinking_face: 

alex_m: Options for short-term mitigation:
- Lower max_microbatch to 4 on hot pools
- Adjust autoscaler to prefer smaller instance increments (add 1-2 nodes sooner)
- Preload KV with last-10 reqs sample when a replica comes up
Which is everyone leaning toward for a fast rollbackable change?

sam_runtime: +1 to lowering microbatch as quickest. We will lose some throughput though. Alternatively make kernel-selector aware of cold-cache mode and prefer kernels optimized for small batches — requires profiling and a small runtime change.

maya_r: Quick canary plan: set `max_microbatch: 4` and `kv_prewarm: true` on a 10% canary pool during peak window for 2h. If p95 stays <120ms and p99 improves, roll. I'll run the canary at 12:30 PT tomorrow. Config diff I will apply looks like:

```
pool.hotspot.canary:
  max_microbatch: 4
  kv_prewarm: true
  prewarm_sample_size: 10
```

alex_m: Add rollout guardrails: p95 < 120ms and cost delta < +8% over 30m or auto-rollback. I'll open the rollout PR and tag infra. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rollouts/1234 (will update)

sre-bot: Alert: p99 > 800ms at 2026-03-16T12:15:46Z (incident-id: spike-20260316-1215)

jia_w: I'll revert the CI change that disabled tile optimizations — there was a comment about toolchain incompatibility on 12.x, but we can gate it per-arch. If we can re-enable optimized kernels that will reduce generic fallback risk during scale-up.

alex_m: Thanks — plan for short-term canary + prewarm, medium-term re-enable tile-opts, long-term improve kernel-selector to be cold-cache aware. I'll summarize in the runtime RFC doc and link follow-ups.

(End of thread)
